Figure 2:Overview of StreamDuo. Top: on an unseen game, the commentator asks the frozen research agent with
the current frames, and the wiki entry it returns two seconds later lets the commentator name what is on
screen. Bottom left: Stage 1 labels an ask only where an answer would make the human line more likely.
Bottom right: Stage 2 distills a frozen copy of the commentator that sees the ideal answer into the
student that sees the noisy one.

Figure 5:Examples on unseen games, with the frame at the second the research agent’s answer arrives. Orange
entries are used by the commentator, and gray ones are not. Proact-VL is retrained on the same data and shown
at the same seconds, and names from Baldur’s Gate 3 are in red.

Figure 6:More examples from the ten unseen games, with StreamDuo and Proact-VL at the same seconds (1/2).
Chips: the entries in the research agent’s answer, in orange those the commentator names. Red: names from
Baldur’s Gate 3.
Figure 7:More examples from the ten unseen games (2/2).
